commit_message:
[CUDA] Raise the default PTX level for sm_89, sm_120 and sm_121 (#24976)

Pick the default per architecture: 8.8 for sm_121, 8.7 for sm_120 and
8.4 for sm_89. An explicit --iree-cuda-target-features can still
override this.

The CUDA target always passes an explicit PTX level to the NVPTX backend
and only raised the +ptx76 default to 7.8 for sm_89. That is below what
the backend accepts for Blackwell, so `--iree-cuda-target=sm_120`
(minimum 8.7) and `sm_121` (minimum 8.8) failed for every program, and
below what the FP8 mma.sync intrinsics selected by default on Ada need,
so an f8E4M3FN matmul on sm_89 failed to select
`llvm.nvvm.mma.m16n8k32.row.col.f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32` (PTX 8.4).

Fixes #24959

Assisted-by: Claude Code

commit_message:
[Bazel] use execution paths for genrule inputs

IREE's shared genrule definitions use rootpath for source files and
execpath for generated files so CMake can distinguish source and build
directories. In Bazel, however, rootpath describes runtime runfiles paths,
which break external IREE builds without legacy runfiles. Translate these
to execpath in the Bazel macro so build actions can locate their inputs.
Existing standalone IREE rules and CMake behavior remain unchanged.

execpath for generated files so CMake can distinguish source and build

commit_message:
fix(PackConstants): don't start new storage buffer if current one is still empty (#23927)

The PackConstants pass introduces a new buffer when a constant cannot be
packed into the current buffer without exceeding the maximum size.
However, if a constant is itself larger than the limit, it gets still
added, but in a separate buffer.
This change fixes a bug in the packing logic when a constant bigger than
the limit is encountered when the current buffer is still empty. In this
case, the current buffer stayed empty and the big constant got added to
a new buffer. The empty buffer caused errors of size 0 buffers not being
supported in following passes or in the runtime. This change avoids
adding a new buffer is the current one is empty and thus avoids these
errors.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
fix(PackConstants): don't start new storage buffer if current one is still empty (#23927)

The PackConstants pass introduces a new buffer when a constant cannot be
packed into the current buffer without exceeding the maximum size.
However, if a constant is itself larger than the limit, it gets still
added, but in a separate buffer.
This change fixes a bug in the packing logic when a constant bigger than
the limit is encountered when the current buffer is still empty. In this
case, the current buffer stayed empty and the big constant got added to
a new buffer. The empty buffer caused errors of size 0 buffers not being
supported in following passes or in the runtime. This change avoids
adding a new buffer is the current one is empty and thus avoids these
errors.

commit_message:
fix(PackConstants): don't start new storage buffer if current one is still empty (#23927)

The PackConstants pass introduces a new buffer when a constant cannot be
packed into the current buffer without exceeding the maximum size.
However, if a constant is itself larger than the limit, it gets still
added, but in a separate buffer.
This change fixes a bug in the packing logic when a constant bigger than
the limit is encountered when the current buffer is still empty. In this
case, the current buffer stayed empty and the big constant got added to
a new buffer. The empty buffer caused errors of size 0 buffers not being
supported in following passes or in the runtime. This change avoids
adding a new buffer is the current one is empty and thus avoids these
errors.

commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its generated
dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers are not exposed
as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel therefore need to maintain
their own build definitions to package Python bindings that match the compiler
they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler packages
against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding definitions alongside
the sources they describe. The bindings use `IREECompiler`'s shared C API so
Python code can inspect and construct IR, then invoke the compiler using the
same MLIR implementation. Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

Assisted-By: GPT-6-Astra

commit_message:
[VM] Preserve 64-bit values in internal calls (#24946)

Internal calls marshaled one 32-bit register per argument and result, so
the high word of a 64-bit value was dropped or overwritten by the next
argument. When that value feeds a buffer bound it surfaces in HAL
command buffer validation as an out-of-range binding, as seen in #24929.

Marshal each argument and result at its full width from the callee's
calling convention, and align argument registers to match how external
calls and imports are already marshaled.

Adds call_ops.vmasm cases for consecutive i64 arguments, i64 results,
and mixed primitive/ref calls. The full VM bytecode test suite passes,
and the repro from #24929, which aborted with OUT_OF_RANGE before the
fix, now returns the expected output.

Fixes #24929

Signed-off-by: zhangpan <98025960+zhangpan2001@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: OpenAI <noreply@openai.com>

commit_message:
[Bazel] Resolve IREE paths and labels in external consumers (#24977)

Bzlmod consumers may embed IREE under a different path or repository
name. Resolving IREE-owned targets and bundled sources in the
consumer's workspace can break repository setup and target loading
for the consumer.
    
The following PR adds the use of Labels(..) so those references
can stay attached to IREE while consumer-provided
dependencies and LLVM tools keep their caller-relative meaning.

Bzlmod consumers may embed IREE under a different path or repository
name. Resolving IREE-owned targets and bundled sources in the
consumer's workspace can break repository setup and target loading
for the consumer.
    
The following PR adds the use of Labels(..) so those references
can stay attached to IREE while consumer-provided
dependencies and LLVM tools keep their caller-relative meaning.

Assisted-by: GPT-Astra-6

commit_message:
[CUDA] Raise the default PTX level for sm_89, sm_120 and sm_121 (#24976)

Pick the default per architecture: 8.8 for sm_121, 8.7 for sm_120 and
8.4 for sm_89. An explicit --iree-cuda-target-features can still
override this.

The CUDA target always passes an explicit PTX level to the NVPTX backend
and only raised the +ptx76 default to 7.8 for sm_89. That is below what
the backend accepts for Blackwell, so `--iree-cuda-target=sm_120`
(minimum 8.7) and `sm_121` (minimum 8.8) failed for every program, and
below what the FP8 mma.sync intrinsics selected by default on Ada need,
so an f8E4M3FN matmul on sm_89 failed to select
`llvm.nvvm.mma.m16n8k32.row.col.f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32` (PTX 8.4).

Fixes #24959

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Samarth Narang <sn2910@nyu.edu>
name: linux-aarch64 :: Build py-compiler-pkg Package

below what the FP8 mma.sync intrinsics selected by default on Ada need,
so an f8E4M3FN matmul on sm_89 failed to select
`llvm.nvvm.mma.m16n8k32.row.col.f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32` (PTX 8.4).

commit_message:
[CUDA] Raise the default PTX level for sm_89, sm_120 and sm_121 (#24976)

Pick the default per architecture: 8.8 for sm_121, 8.7 for sm_120 and
8.4 for sm_89. An explicit --iree-cuda-target-features can still
override this.

The CUDA target always passes an explicit PTX level to the NVPTX backend
and only raised the +ptx76 default to 7.8 for sm_89. That is below what
the backend accepts for Blackwell, so `--iree-cuda-target=sm_120`
(minimum 8.7) and `sm_121` (minimum 8.8) failed for every program, and
below what the FP8 mma.sync intrinsics selected by default on Ada need,
so an f8E4M3FN matmul on sm_89 failed to select
`llvm.nvvm.mma.m16n8k32.row.col.f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32` (PTX 8.4).

Fixes #24959

Assisted-by: Claude Code

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a938559a9145 (#24982)

Updates LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a938559a9145, retaining the GPU
min/maxnumf carry patch from llvm/llvm-project#226903.

Compatibility changes:

- Bump StableHLO to openxla/stablehlo@c2eaf28a to pick up compatibility
with strict property assembly formats (llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4).
  Upstream also covers these previously carried IREE fixes:
  - Migrate complex element handling to `mlir::Complex`
    (iree-org/stablehlo@28549ef5).
  - Remove obsolete DenseMap empty/tombstone key handling
    (iree-org/stablehlo@a2727e57).
  - Preserve enum assembly syntax without angle brackets
    (iree-org/stablehlo@50a9d75a).
- Temporarily opt affected IREE dialects and Torch-MLIR TMTensor out of
  strict property assembly formats to preserve existing syntax
  (llvm/llvm-project@c495a9b796c4).
- Replace `checkParallelRegions` with `mayHaveParallelRegions`,
preserving
  existing bufferization behavior (llvm/llvm-project@d6048f5ff3bd).
- Use DataLayout-aware constant GEP construction in LLVMCPU
  (llvm/llvm-project@2a6247359ee5).
- Keep widening visible through shape casts for CPU custom kernels and
  SPIR-V dot products after (llvm/llvm-project@2c298348bfe1)
- Update the TOSA constant check for its new assembly format
  (llvm/llvm-project@fe5ace607b58)
- Carry the MMA slice-cache correction for the regression introduced 
  by (llvm/llvm-project@d287e55d0302)

Assisted-by: Codex

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Add RISC-V V f32 vfmacc.vf inner_tiled MMA. (#24933)

## Summary

Lowers RISC-V V f32 `inner_tiled` MMA (`MMA_RISCV_V_VFMACC_*_F32_F32`)
to
`llvm.riscv.vfmacc` (`vfmacc.vf`). Tile N is `vlen/8`. Introduces shared
helper
`lowerRiscvVFmaccLike`.

This is the first stacked dtype PR from #24926 review. Performance will
be tracked here #24932

Assisted-by: Cursor

Towards: #24311

---------

commit_message:
[Bazel] Resolve IREE paths and labels in external consumers (#24977)

Bzlmod consumers may embed IREE under a different path or repository
name. Resolving IREE-owned targets and bundled sources in the
consumer's workspace can break repository setup and target loading
for the consumer.
    
The following PR adds the use of Labels(..) so those references
can stay attached to IREE while consumer-provided
dependencies and LLVM tools keep their caller-relative meaning.

Assisted-by: GPT-Astra-6

commit_message:
[VM] Preserve 64-bit values in internal calls (#24946)

Internal calls marshaled one 32-bit register per argument and result, so
the high word of a 64-bit value was dropped or overwritten by the next
argument. When that value feeds a buffer bound it surfaces in HAL
command buffer validation as an out-of-range binding, as seen in #24929.

Marshal each argument and result at its full width from the callee's
calling convention, and align argument registers to match how external
calls and imports are already marshaled.

Adds call_ops.vmasm cases for consecutive i64 arguments, i64 results,
and mixed primitive/ref calls. The full VM bytecode test suite passes,
and the repro from #24929, which aborted with OUT_OF_RANGE before the
fix, now returns the expected output.

Fixes #24929

Signed-off-by: zhangpan <98025960+zhangpan2001@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: OpenAI <noreply@openai.com>
name: Test Torch / test_torch_ops :: amdgpu_hip_gfx1100_O3

commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its generated
dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers are not exposed
as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel therefore need to maintain
their own build definitions to package Python bindings that match the compiler
they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler packages
against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding definitions alongside
the sources they describe. The bindings use `IREECompiler`'s shared C API so
Python code can inspect and construct IR, then invoke the compiler using the
same MLIR implementation. Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

Assisted-By: GPT-6-Astra

commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its generated
dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers are not exposed
as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel therefore need to maintain
their own build definitions to package Python bindings that match the compiler
they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler packages
against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding definitions alongside
the sources they describe. The bindings use `IREECompiler`'s shared C API so
Python code can inspect and construct IR, then invoke the compiler using the
same MLIR implementation. Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

commit_message:
fix(PackConstants): don't start new storage buffer if current one is still empty (#23927)

The PackConstants pass introduces a new buffer when a constant cannot be
packed into the current buffer without exceeding the maximum size.
However, if a constant is itself larger than the limit, it gets still
added, but in a separate buffer.
This change fixes a bug in the packing logic when a constant bigger than
the limit is encountered when the current buffer is still empty. In this
case, the current buffer stayed empty and the big constant got added to
a new buffer. The empty buffer caused errors of size 0 buffers not being
supported in following passes or in the runtime. This change avoids
adding a new buffer is the current one is empty and thus avoids these
errors.

commit_message:
[Bazel] use execution paths for genrule inputs

IREE's shared genrule definitions use rootpath for source files and
execpath for generated files so CMake can distinguish source and build
directories. In Bazel, however, rootpath describes runtime runfiles paths,
which break external IREE builds without legacy runfiles. Translate these
to execpath in the Bazel macro so build actions can locate their inputs.
Existing standalone IREE rules and CMake behavior remain unchanged.
